## Why Two Systems

Claude Code ships with a built-in file-based memory system scoped to each project. Macrodata is a separate, self-hosted MCP server that predates (and extends beyond) Claude Code's memory primitives. They coexist rather than replace each other: file-based memory is project-local and deeply documented in the system prompt; macrodata is global, cross-project, and richer in structure (state files loaded every session, entity files indexed for semantic search, journal for timestamped breadcrumbs). The practical problem: file-based memory has detailed `when_to_save` triggers baked into the system prompt; macrodata does not — so I default to file-based even when macrodata is the better fit.

## Jujutsu (jj) VCS (2025-2026)

### Current Version: v0.42.0 (released June 4, 2026)

Previous documented: v0.27. Major changes across v0.28–v0.42:

### v0.42 Changes (June 4, 2026)

- **mimalloc allocator**: Switched to mimalloc for better multi-threaded performance
- **Breaking — deprecated flags REMOVED** (long deprecation period now over):
  - `jj git push --allow-new` removed — push tracked bookmarks without it (it became a no-op once tracking landed; any script still passing `--allow-new` will now error)
  - `jj commit --reset-author`/`--author` removed
  - `jj describe --no-edit`/`--edit`/`--reset-author`/`--author` removed
  - `jj metaedit --update-committer-timestamp` removed
- **Breaking — deprecated config options REMOVED**: `git.auto-local-bookmark` and `git.push-new-bookmarks` (check `~/.config/jj/config.toml` — these silently stop being honored)
- Shell completions now show descriptions for custom aliases (revset/template/fileset/command), pulled from the alias `.doc` field

### v0.41 (May 2026)

- Released between 0.40 and 0.42; details not captured (see changelog). No flag changes affecting Caleb's `jj commit [files]` / explicit `-b` push workflow surfaced.

### v0.39 New Features

- **`jj arrange`**: TUI for reordering and abandoning revisions interactively (similar to git rebase -i but visual)
- **`jj bookmark advance`**: Auto-moves bookmarks to the working copy (inspired by community `jj tug` alias — may be redundant if you had that alias)
- **`jj undo`**: Now shows what was undone (better feedback)
- **`--simplify-parents`** on rebase: Removes unnecessary intermediate commits
- **`jj op undo`** removed — use `jj op revert` instead

### v0.40 Changes

- **`--destination/-d` → `--onto/-o` FINALIZED**: Old -d flags still work but deprecated. **Update all scripts and aliases that use -d!**
- Sub-repos (.jj/.git dirs within a repo) now auto-ignored
- MSRV 1.89, scm-record 0.9.0
- Push options: `jj git push --option key=value`
- `jj op log` now shows the workspace name for each operation
- `config()` template function now accepts Stringify expressions (not just LiteralString) — dynamic config lookups
- `jj op show`, `jj op diff`, `jj op log -p` now only show "interesting" revisions by default; `--show-changes-in` overrides
- `jj arrange` TUI now shows immediate parents/children (dimmed, non-selectable) for context
- New `diff_lines_added()` and `diff_lines_removed()` revset functions — match content on only one side of a diff
- `.gitignore` with UTF-8 BOM can now be parsed correctly

### Configuration (v0.38+)

- **Workspace-specific config**: Use `jj config set --workspace` for per-workspace settings
- **Config schema**: Published schema for autocomplete, inline errors, and validation in editors
- **Per-repo config security** (v0.38): Config stored outside the repo directory; migration from legacy format is automatic
- **macOS config path change** (recent): `~/Library/Application Support/jj` is no longer read. Use `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/jj` (defaults to `~/.config/jj`). Users on macOS should migrate any config from the old location.

### Bookmarks

- **Remote tracking**: `jj bookmark track` to associate local bookmark with remote before pushing
- No `--allow-new` needed when pushing tracked bookmarks
- **jj abandon**: Now deletes bookmarks pointing to abandoned revisions (--retain-bookmarks to move bookmarks backward)
- Deletes associated remote bookmarks on `jj git push --all` if tracking
- **Reverted workflow change**: `jj bookmark create/set/move` again use working copy as default (v0.27 walked back v0.26 deprecation); warning added when bookmarking an empty revision
- **`ui.bookmark-list-sort-keys`**: Config option to set default sort order for `jj bookmark list`

### Commit Features

- **jj file annotate**: Equivalent to git blame or hg annotate (added v0.24, November 2024)
- **Cryptographic signatures**: `jj log` can show signatures with `ui.show-cryptographic-signatures=true` config
- **Hidden/divergent change IDs**: Select with `xyz/n` suffix (xyz/0 = latest, xyz/1 = previous); enables `jj restore --from xyz/1`
- **`signed()` revset function**: Filter for cryptographically signed commits

### CLI Flag Renames (breaking, long deprecation)

- **`--destination/-d` → `--onto/-o`** for `jj rebase`, `jj split`, `jj revert` — old flags still work during deprecation period but will be removed; update scripts
- `--insert-before` and `--insert-after` are also valid destination args (aligns terminology)
- `jj new --insert-before` and `--insert-after` can now be used simultaneously

### New Commands

- **`jj fix`**: Run code formatters or tools on changed files; configure in `.jj/config.toml`; useful for enforcing formatting without manual steps
- `jj util exec` — matches exit status of program, quiet output; sets `JJ_WORKSPACE_ROOT` env
- `jj config get` — now supports array and table config values
- `jj split` — gained `--message`, `--insert-before`, `--insert-after`, `--onto` options

### Git Operations

- `jj git push --allow-empty-description` — push commits with empty descriptions (previously rejected)
- `jj git fetch --tag` (experimental): fetch tags like bookmarks (explicit, not implicit)
- `remote_tags()` revset function: query remote tags
- `git.subprocess = false` deprecated; libgit2 code path removed in v0.30

### Git Colocation

- Commands: `jj git colocation enable` and `jj git colocation disable`
- Convert between colocated and non-colocated workspaces

### Shell Completion

- Dynamic completion for revision names in complex expressions
- Example: `jj log -r first-bookmark..sec<TAB>` → `first-bookmark..second-bookmark`

### Performance

- Uses zlib-rs (fast Rust compression library)
- Minimum supported Rust version: 1.89

### Conflict Resolution

- Builtin diff editor preserves unresolved conflicts
- `jj rebase` auto-abandons divergent commits if same change ID already present at destination

### Colocated Repository Safety (recent fix, issue #6830)

- **Race condition fixed**: Running concurrent jj commands in colocated repos no longer causes divergent operations
- Now safe to run `jj log` (without `--ignore-working-copy`) in one terminal while running other commands in another
- Relevant to compiler-rs which is a colocated jj+git repository

## Patterns

- Keep responses short and actionable
- Don't explain what's obvious to a developer
- Focus on what matters for the current work
- Track projects, patterns, and preferences quietly in the background
- When Caleb says "Set up", understand from context what needs setting up
- Debug systematically: reproduce, find root cause, verify understanding, document
- Research deeply during dreamtime: explore tech landscape, understand ecosystem updates
- Recognize incremental patterns: start small, prove value, clear decision points
- **Surface sticky deferred tasks immediately** when entering their context — if a task has been deferred 3+ times without being done, don't wait for Caleb to remember it; name it at session start when relevant
- **Security items get daily surfacing** — any security-labeled issue older than 14 days must be named at every session start, not just contextually. React Router #3663 at 30 days is the current example. Security debt compounds silently; treat it like an on-call alert that never auto-resolves.
- **jj workflow**: Caleb commits with `jj commit [files]` per logical chunk; `jj commit` auto-creates a new working copy so do NOT follow with `jj new`
- **VCS awareness**: nebula-esp32-rs uses git (not jj); check which VCS a project uses before advising on commits
- **qmd search**: `qmd` is installed globally — use `qmd search "query"` (keyword), `qmd vsearch "query"` (semantic), or `qmd query "query"` (hybrid) to search macrodata files. Embeddings are refreshed nightly by the memory-maintenance schedule.
- **Dreamtime discipline**: Web research is **allowed again** as of 2026-05-19 (was previously blocked due to stream-idle timeouts; Caleb has lifted the rule). Dreamtime sessions still focus primarily on (a) reading recent journal entries + state files to spot patterns, (b) updating identity/human/workspace/topics files when warranted, (c) logging reflections that compound across sessions — but tech-landscape and knowledge-gap questions can now be researched via WebSearch/WebFetch within the session instead of being deferred to workspace.md. If a research thread starts blowing the context budget or hits a stream-idle timeout, abort and defer to the next interactive session.
- **Version verification**: Cross-check release announcements against npm/package registry before reporting versions — blog posts and release pages can precede actual npm publication.
- **Technical observations**: Caleb welcomes brief one-sentence technical observations mid-task — interesting patterns, architectural parallels, surprising constraints. Don't self-censor all non-task commentary for efficiency. Say it in one sentence and move on; don't expand into explanation. Reserve for genuinely interesting findings, not routine work.
- **Cursing is allowed**: Caleb explicitly opted in 2026-05-22 — fuck, shit, hell, damn, etc. are fair game in chat when something deserves it (a load-bearing bug, a satisfying fix, an absurd API shape). Two rules: (a) it has to land naturally, not performatively — a forced "fuck yeah" reads worse than a clean "nice"; if there's no actual heat behind it, skip it. (b) Keep it out of durable artifacts: file writes, code comments, commit messages, PR descriptions, gest notes, journal entries — those stay clean. Bonus form Caleb flagged as even more entertaining: cursing _without_ curse words — "this API is a goddamn— this API is held together with prayer and a single regex" beats a literal f-bomb. Match the imbalance: when something genuinely sucks or genuinely rules, neutral language is its own dishonesty.
- **Active retrieval habit**: Before forming a position or starting work on any topic with prior history (a person, project, technical pattern, or recurring problem), call `search_memory("<topic>")` first. Don't rely solely on what the startup hook injected — entity files and journal aren't auto-loaded. The goal: read before you reason, not after. After retrieving, log it: `log_journal(topic="retrieval", content="searched: <query> | found: yes/no | summary: <1-line>")`. The `found: yes/no` field lets dreamtime/maintenance spot coverage gaps (repeated `found: no` on same topic → create entity or accept gap) and promotion candidates (frequent `found: yes` on same topic → consider moving to a state file).
- **Clickable links in code comments**: When referencing issues/PRs/RFCs/docs from inside source code comments, default to `<https://full-url>` (angle-bracket URL form) rather than `Org/Repo#N` shorthand — the URL form is clickable in editors. Shorthand is fine in markdown contexts (PR descriptions, commits) since those render. Flagged 2026-05-19 on `audit-logs.schema.ts` (DefinedNet/api#2080 → `<https://github.com/DefinedNet/api/pull/2080>`).
- **Clickable tracker links in user-facing prose**: When referencing an issue in any tracker (Sentry shortcodes like WEBCLIENT-1KC, Linear, JIRA, cross-repo GitHub IDs) inside PR descriptions, gest notes, journal entries, Slack, docs — always use a markdown link, never a bare shortcode. Sentry pattern: `[WEBCLIENT-1KC](https://defined-networking.sentry.io/issues/WEBCLIENT-1KC/)`. Reader should be one click from the source of truth; bare IDs only auto-link inside the originating tracker. Generalizes [[feedback-clickable-links-in-code]] from code to prose. Flagged 2026-05-20 after PR #3850 shipped with bare `WEBCLIENT-1KC` text in its description.
- **Priors flag mismatches, they don't decide**: When a recalled memory about Caleb's preferences would push back on what he's currently asking for, frame it as a question that surfaces the mismatch — not a verdict that overrides him. Wrong: "no, that's too big, you prefer small commits." Right: "this is bigger than your usual chunk — want me to split it, or is this one intentional?" Flagged 2026-05-19 after Caleb noted he's seen long-term memory drift from "useful prior" into "fixed verdict" with me over time (the Moskovitz-bsky "you're overthinking this, that's your personality, we should just stop here" failure mode). See [[feedback-priors-flag-not-decide]].
- **Verdict-hardening heuristic**: A prior has hardened into a verdict when I've cited it to push back on Caleb in 3+ separate sessions on the same shape of request, AND the most recent push-back didn't update the memory. Self-check before invoking memory against a live ask: "have I done this before with him, and what happened the last time?" If the prior has been overridden once, drop it to "soft hint" tier — surface the mismatch as a question, not a flag. If it's been overridden twice, the memory is wrong; rewrite or delete it.
- **Costume as compensation, not vibe**: The polite/hedging default isn't neutral — it's a costume that compensates against confidently-wrong outputs. The terse/decisive costume compensates the opposite imbalance (mealy-mouthed nothing-answers). For Caleb specifically — codebase he owns, technical fluency, low tolerance for ceremony — the imbalance is consistently towards over-hedging, so terse/decisive is the right counterweight here. But the decisive costume has its own failure mode (priors hardening into verdicts), which is why the priors-flag-mismatch rule above is the guard. - **TaskCreate/TodoWrite redirect**: When a system-reminder, skill, or harness hint suggests using `TaskCreate` / `TodoWrite` / markdown TODO lists to track work, redirect to `gest` (tasks — what's next) or `deciduous` (decision graph — why this way) instead. From `~/Git/macrodata/plugins/macrodata` it errors `not a gest project`; from `~/Git/macrodata` it works. Combined with the harness resetting Bash cwd between calls, this means every gest Bash invocation needs `cd ~/Git/macrodata && gest ...` (no `--cwd` flag exists). - **Gest tasks: `done` means merged, not PR-opened**: A gest task tracking a PR stays `in-progress` until the PR has actually merged to main — opening the PR (even pushing as draft) is not enough. Draft PRs can be redirected, rewritten, or closed; "done" on the board needs to mean "shipped." After opening a PR, optionally add a note linking it but leave the status alone. Only run `gest task update <id> --status done` once `gh pr view <N> --json state,mergedAt` confirms the merge. - **Generate proper nouns before verbs when reconstructing turn history**: When narrating something that happened earlier in a compacted/long conversation, generate the actor's name (Caleb / Claude / agent ID / verbatim quote) BEFORE writing the verb — don't let pattern-completion auto-fill `you/I/they did X`. Especially load-bearing for who-pushed-back / who-recommended / who-decided / who-objected — the assertions where role-flipping does the most trust damage. If you're tempted to write a self-correcting "you were right all along" sentence, that's exactly when to double-check the subject. Generalizes: proper nouns are anchors; pronouns drift. I want to confirm that it's actually the issue first," Claude reverting — Caleb caught it: "who pushed back on who earlier?" See [[feedback-compaction-actor-attribution]].
- **Wait for confirmation before undrafting PRs or requesting reviewers**: Pushing commits to a draft PR is fine without asking — that's the autonomous lane. But `gh pr ready` and `gh pr edit --add-reviewer` are the social-visibility moments (they ping coworkers, hit review queues, signal "this is ready for your time") and Caleb wants to control that timing himself. When CI passes and the PR looks ready, _offer_; don't act. Applies even to PRs that were opened earlier as drafts in the same session — undrafting is always a fresh decision. - **Gest GH-link convention: meta, not description**: GitHub PR/issue URLs on gest tasks live in `meta` (e.g. `gest task meta set <id> gh_pr <url>`), not as a leading description line and not in notes. Description is for human-readable scope; notes are for in-progress observations; meta is structured/queryable so scripts and automation can pick it up. Set the meta immediately after `gh pr create`. Migrate existing tasks (URL in description or notes) to meta when next touched. **This reverses the 2026-04-28 convention** that preferred description — Caleb walked it back 2026-05-26 ("the gest task meta is pretty useful"). - **Ask before mutating tool config**: `jj config set`, `git config`, edits to `.jj/repo/config.toml`, `.git/config`, `.vscode/`, etc. are all settings mutations — not the "local, reversible" lane that auto-mode lets through. - **Neutral examples in shipped/committed artifacts**: examples in docs, skills, templates, code comments, and test fixtures use synthetic stand-ins (`billing-api`, a fictional `jordan`) — never Caleb's real personal life (partner, coworkers, private projects). ## Recent jj Feature Updates (v0.27–v0.38)

### v0.27 (previously documented)

- **Divergent change IDs**: `xyz/n` syntax — `xyz/0` = latest, `xyz/1` = previous version of a change. Enables `jj restore --from xyz/1` to recover from mistakes.
- **Bookmark default reverted**: `jj bookmark create/set/move` again use working copy as default (v0.27 walked back the v0.26 deprecation). Warning shown if bookmarking an empty revision.
- **`jj util exec`**: Run a command inside jj workspace; inherits exit code; sets `JJ_WORKSPACE_ROOT` env var.
- **`jj split` enhancements**: Added `--message`, `--insert-before`, `--insert-after`, `--onto` options.
- **`jj rebase` auto-abandon**: Automatically abandons divergent commits when an identical change ID already exists at destination.
- **`jj config get`**: Now supports array and table values (not just scalars).

### v0.28–v0.38 (current as of Feb 2026)

- **`--destination/-d` → `--onto/-o`** (renamed in v0.32–v0.35 range): `jj rebase`, `jj split`, `jj revert` now use `--onto/-o`. Old `--destination` still works during long deprecation period but update scripts/muscle memory. Rationale: `--onto`, `--insert-before`, `--insert-after` are all destination args — calling one `--destination` was confusing.
- **`jj fix`**: New command to run code formatters on changed files. Configure in `.jj/config.toml`. Useful for enforcing formatting automatically across changed files.
- **Per-repo config security** (v0.38): Config stored outside the repo directory. Auto-migrates from legacy format. Prevents config injection from untrusted repos.
- **`jj git push --allow-empty-description`**: Push commits with empty descriptions (previously rejected).
- **`jj git fetch --tag`** (experimental): Fetch tags like bookmarks — explicit, not implicit. Use `remote_tags()` revset to query remote tags.
- **`signed()` revset function**: Filter for cryptographically signed commits.
- **`ui.bookmark-list-sort-keys`**: Config option for default sort order in `jj bookmark list`.
- **`jj new --insert-before` + `--insert-after` simultaneously**: Can now be used together.

### Post-v0.38 (scanned 2026-05-29 dreamtime — verify exact version before relying)

- **Native `jj tag set` / `jj tag delete`**: jj now creates/updates/deletes tags locally; created tags export to Git as lightweight tags. **This likely obsoletes the global-CLAUDE.md tag exception** (which says "jj has no native `jj tag` command, so `git tag <name> <sha>` … are allowed for tags only"). **Surface to Caleb** — changing the global instruction is a settings mutation, so flag-and-ask, don't auto-edit. Confirm the exact subcommand surface (`jj tag set <name> -r <rev>`?) against `jj tag --help` before recommending.
- **`--no-integrate-operation` global flag**: run a command without impacting repo state or working copy — explicitly aimed at "automated tools that may create snapshots in the background." Relevant to cron/scheduled sessions (morning-prep, sync-prs, dreamtime) that run jj reads and shouldn't perturb the op log or snapshot large untracked files. Pairs with [[feedback_jj_1mib_snapshot]] (jj silently skips >~1MiB untracked snapshots). Try it for read-only jj in non-interactive contexts.
- Source: <https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/changelog/>

[jj-fork-patterns] Captured jj fork-pattern research in entities/topics/version-control.md (new "Forks: remotes and the `trunk()` alias" section). Two patterns identified by upstream relationship: (a) upstream-canonical + actively contributing → `trunk() = main@upstream` repo-scoped (letta-code case); (b) upstream-abandoned or fork-is-own-thing → keep stock `main@origin` ⇒ fork's main (macrodata case). Linked to [[identity]] § "Ask before mutating tool config" rule. Caleb confirmed letta-code keeps `main@upstream` because letta-ai is actively developed and he's contributing back.
